text: A Full Moon is the Moon at its brightest, standing opposite the Sun at the peak of the lunar month, and whatever house holds it gets flooded with light. About once a year that house is your first, the one that covers your body, your bearing, and the name people know you by. So the lit-up thing is you. Feelings you have been carrying quietly climb to the surface and show on your face, and people who usually miss your moods suddenly read them clearly. Personal matters that have been building for months reach full size in these few days: a change of direction declares itself, a question about who you are becoming demands an answer, an effort that carries your name comes back with results. Because the Sun shines from the opposite side of your chart, the side of partners and close others, much of the light arrives through relationships. Someone reflects you back at full strength, agrees or objects, and the pull between what you want and what they need can stretch tight. That tension is not a malfunction; it is how this moon shows you where you end and others begin. Emotion runs high while it lasts, and decisions made at the top of the wave can be truer than usual or simply louder, so it helps to know which you are hearing. The useful work is mostly witnessing: seeing plainly what months of small choices about yourself have added up to, and letting anything overripe be finished. Within a few days the light drops and the volume with it, but what you saw about yourself stays seen. Since a Full Moon visits this house about yearly, you get a regular appointment with your own reflection. Over the years those appointments teach you to meet your own visibility without flinching, and to treat the strong feelings of these days as a reading of where you stand rather than a command to act on the spot.

Once a year or so, the lunar month reaches its full point in your second house, which holds your income, your belongings, and whatever you count as valuable. At a Full Moon the Moon faces the Sun across the sky and reflects its whole light, so matters ripen and show their results; here, the results are material. A money question that has been developing for months comes due in some visible way: a payment lands or a bill does, a purchase completes, a negotiation over pay or price reaches its moment of truth. Even when nothing dramatic happens on paper, you can see your material life with unusual clarity for a few days: what you own, what you owe, what your effort has actually earned. Feelings run close to the money now. Security worries swell in the bright light, and so does pleasure in what you have, so the same evening can hold both gratitude and alarm. Because the Sun stands in the opposite house, the territory of shared money and other people's resources, questions of yours and theirs come into the same frame: a debt between you and someone else, a partner's finances touching your own, what you carry jointly against what you keep in your name. Choices about worth surface too, and not only in prices. What you will trade your time for, what you refuse to sell, which comforts are worth their cost: those valuations show themselves in full light, and one of them may clearly need revising. This is a better moment for taking honest stock than for large new commitments, since the feelings inflating around money will settle within days while the facts remain. The moon returns to this house about yearly, and each pass is a harvest report on the material thread of your life. Read year against year, it shows you slowly what your relationship with having and earning is actually doing, which is the first thing you need in order to steer it.

Every month the Moon comes to fullness somewhere in your chart, and roughly once a year it does so in your third house, the house of words, siblings and neighbors, short trips, and daily information. A Full Moon is the middle of the lunar cycle, the point of most light, when things that have been building become visible and complete. Here, what completes is usually said. A conversation you have been postponing finally happens. News arrives that settles a question. Something you wrote, taught, or promised comes back with a response, and you find out how it landed. The mental weather turns loud for a few days: more messages, more errands, more people needing an answer, and your own thoughts running quicker and closer to your feelings than usual. Words carry extra charge under this light. You may say the true thing with unusual ease, or say the sharp thing with unusual speed, and the difference often comes down to whether you pause before sending. Siblings, cousins, neighbors, the people woven into your ordinary rounds, can step forward now with something that needs airing, and old threads of conversation reach their natural end. Because the Sun sits in the opposite house, the house of big pictures and far horizons, these days often stage a meeting between the grand view and the near detail: a belief tested by a plain fact, a plan forced to answer practical questions. The work that suits the moment is finishing and delivering rather than drafting: sending the letter, closing the loop, saying the thing cleanly. Then the noise drops. Since this moon returns to the house about once a year, it acts as an annual audit of how you speak and listen, and over time it teaches a durable skill: letting strong feeling into your words without letting it drive.

Home is where this one lands. About once a year the Full Moon, the bright midpoint of the lunar month when the Moon faces the Sun and matters ripen, falls in your fourth house, the house of home, family, and your private foundations. For a few days the deepest layer of your life is the loudest. Feelings about family, about where you live and where you come from, rise with unusual force, and household business that has been simmering reaches its visible conclusion: a move completes, a repair finishes or finally demands attention, a family question that everyone has been circling gets said out loud. Old material surfaces easily under this light. A parent or an elder may be on your mind, memories arrive uninvited, and you can find yourself moved by small domestic things, a room at dusk, a familiar meal, out of proportion to their size. That is the house doing its work: showing you what home actually means to you now, as opposed to what it used to mean. Because the Sun stands opposite, in the house of career and public life, the old tug between the job and the hearth often tightens for a few days, and something has to be chosen, even if only an evening. The feeling half of you tends to win this round, and mostly should. What suits these days is tending: being in the place you live, feeding the people in it, finishing the domestic thing that is nearly done, letting the emotion move through instead of managing it flat. The tide recedes on schedule. A Full Moon lights this house about once a year, so the reading of your foundations comes around again and again, and across years the readings add up: you learn what actually steadies you, which family patterns are yours to keep, and which came due long ago and can finally be set down.

Roughly once a year, the Full Moon arrives in your fifth house, the house of pleasure, romance, children, and the things you make. Full Moons are culminations: the Moon stands opposite the Sun, fully lit, and whatever has been growing in the house it occupies comes into plain view. Here, the harvest is personal and warm. Something you made gets seen: shared, performed, shown to the person whose opinion matters. A romance reaches a threshold where it wants to be named, one way or the other. If children are part of your life, one of them steps into the light with a milestone, a need, or a performance of their own. Even in a quiet year, the appetite for delight peaks: you want the evening out, the game, the color, the thing done purely because it pleases you. Feelings run theatrical for a few days, and pride and vulnerability arrive together, since being seen means being seen. The Sun, meanwhile, shines from the far side of the chart, where friends and the wider group live, so a tension can surface between your own voice and the crowd's taste, between what you love making and what others want from you. This moon tends to side with the personal. The risk of the season is overplaying the moment, betting too much on one night's applause or one flush of romance; the gift is honest evidence, because in full light you can see whether the thing you have been making, or the person you have been becoming around someone, is actually alive. Take the evidence and let the drama pass. With this visitation returning about yearly, your creative and romantic life gets an annual opening night, and over time you learn its lesson by repetition: joy holds up better when you let it be witnessed, and what survives being seen is the part worth keeping.

About once a year a Full Moon culminates in your sixth house, the house of work, routine, and the daily upkeep of your body. At the height of the lunar month the Moon reflects the Sun's whole light and running matters show their results; in this house the results are practical. A stretch of work reaches its deadline or its delivery. The systems you live by, the schedule, the inbox, the chores, hit their point of maximum load, and you can see exactly which routines hold and which buckle. Your body gives its report as well. Weeks of good sleep or bad, movement or none, tend to make themselves felt around now, not as punishment but as information arriving on schedule. Feelings run high in a place that usually keeps them filed, so small frictions at work can swell, and helpers, colleagues, and the people you serve become vivid: appreciation or resentment that has been accumulating in either direction wants acknowledgment. Across the chart the Sun occupies the opposite ground, where retreat and the inner life belong, and the axis makes its old argument: duty against rest, service against solitude. These few days often show you the cost of ignoring either end. What suits the moment is completion and honest maintenance: shipping the nearly-done thing, clearing the backlog, noticing the habit that plainly is not working rather than vowing a whole new regime. Adjustments made from evidence outlast resolutions made from mood. Then the load lightens and the week goes ordinary again. The moon comes back to this house about once a year, an inspection of the machinery of your days. Read over years, it teaches a quiet competence: your routines are choices, your body keeps accurate books, and the daily round works best when it is tended in daylight rather than rescued in crisis.

Once a year or so, a Full Moon rises in your seventh house, the house of partnership: spouses and companions, close collaborators, and the people you face one to one. A Full Moon is a culmination, the moment in the lunar month when the Moon stands opposite the Sun and whatever has been quietly accumulating shows itself whole. Here, what shows itself is the state of a relationship. Something between you and another person reaches its full expression in these few days: a commitment asks to be made explicit, a long negotiation arrives at yes or no, a tension that has been politely managed refuses to stay managed. The other person becomes vivid, easier to see clearly and harder to ignore, and feelings on both sides run at high tide. With the Sun lighting your own end of the axis, the classic question of this house sharpens: how much of you bends to keep the two of you working, and how much of the two of you exists to support each of you. Neither answer wins outright; the moon simply puts the balance on display. Old relational patterns surface too, the moves you make under pressure with any partner, and seeing one operate in real time is worth more than a year of theorizing about it. If you are not partnered, the culmination often comes through a rival, a client, a friend acting as a mirror; the house includes everyone who stands across from you. Little needs deciding at the peak itself. Let the conversation finish, let the truth of where things stand be visible, and give large verdicts a few days to cool. The reading repeats about yearly, a weather report on how you do closeness, and over the years it grows a specific skill: staying yourself at close range, and letting the other person be fully real.

What is shared and what is hidden both live in your eighth house: joint money, debts and legacies, intimacy, and the endings that let life move. About once a year the Full Moon reaches its peak there, and for a few days this quiet territory is fully lit. Full Moons bring things to a head, and in this house the head things come to is often private. A matter of shared resources becomes unavoidable: a loan, a settlement, taxes, an account entangled with someone else's, arriving at its due date or its resolution. Or the culmination is intimate rather than financial: a closeness deepens past the point of casualness, a secret surfaces, a truth between you and someone else stops being deferrable. Emotions here run deep rather than loud. You may feel things during these days with a force that surprises you, grief or desire or old anger, rising as if on a schedule of its own, which in a sense it is. Across the sky the Sun holds your house of personal money and worth, so the axis frames a familiar tension: what is mine, what is ours, what the entanglement costs and what it makes possible. Something usually asks to be released around this moon, a debt in any currency, a grip, a chapter that has quietly been over for a while. Endings under full light are cleaner than endings in the dark, because you can see what you are setting down. There is no need to force one; ripeness does most of the work. When the light passes, the depths close over again, and you carry up whatever you saw. Returning about yearly, this moon gives you a regular meeting with the parts of life that resist small talk, and each pass makes you a little less afraid of them: shared weight, honest need, and the endings that turn out to be doors.

Somewhere beyond your daily round, this one culminates. Roughly once a year the Full Moon lands in your ninth house, the house of far travel, advanced study, publication, and conviction, and the wide-angle side of your life reaches a visible peak. A Full Moon is the lunar month at maximum light, when what has been developing shows its results; here the results concern distance and meaning. A journey happens or completes, or a place far away steps into your week through news, an arrival, an invitation. A course of study reaches its examination or its end. Something you wrote or taught travels beyond your circle and comes back with a verdict. And often the culmination is inward: a belief you have carried reaches its test, holding up in full light or plainly failing to, and you feel the difference at once. Conviction runs hot for a few days. You may find yourself arguing a position with more feeling than the topic seems to warrant, because under this moon opinions are not abstract, they are emotional property. The Sun meanwhile lights the opposite end of the axis, the near and the everyday, and the pairing asks its perennial question: how the big picture squares with the small print, whether the philosophy survives contact with Tuesday. The best use of these days is letting the large thing finish: submitting, concluding, arriving, saying what you now actually think. New doctrines can wait for lower light. As this moon comes back about yearly, it serves as an annual reckoning of the direction your understanding is growing, and over the years it does what the ninth house promises. Your world gets larger, and your convictions, tested regularly in bright light, get fewer and sturdier.

About once a year, the Full Moon culminates in your tenth house, the most public ground in your chart: career, reputation, and the role you hold in the world's eyes. A Full Moon marks the peak of the lunar month, the Moon fully lit opposite the Sun, and in this house the peak happens in front of people. Professional matters that have been building for months arrive at their visible moment: a project launches or lands, a review or announcement comes due, a bid succeeds or plainly does not, your name gets attached to a result. Even in an uneventful year, you can feel unusually seen at work, as if a light swung toward your corner. Feelings about ambition and how far you have come run stronger than a workweek usually allows. Full light flatters and exposes with the same beam. Work that is genuinely done tends to be rewarded now, and gaps that have been papered over tend to show, which makes these days honest more than kind. The Sun sits in the opposite house, the house of home and private life. So the oldest tension in the chart pulls taut: the public role against the private person, what you build outside against what you tend at home. Someone at home may need you precisely when the spotlight arrives; that timing is a feature of the axis, not bad luck. The season favors delivering and acknowledging rather than launching: finish, present, take the credit or the correction, and thank the people under the work. Verdicts about your whole career made at emotional high tide should wait a week. This moon returns about yearly, a results day for your public thread. Its long gift is calibration: year over year you learn what recognition does for you, what it costs, and how much of it you want.

Your eleventh house is where the people who share your causes live: friends, groups, teams, communities, and the hopes you carry about the future. When the Full Moon comes to this house, about once each year, the collective side of your life reaches its bright peak. This is the culminating phase, the Moon at maximum light facing the Sun, and what culminates here usually involves more names than yours. A group effort arrives at its result: the event happens, the campaign concludes, the project the team has carried gets delivered and judged. Friendships reach clarifying moments, a bond deepening into something structural, or a mismatch that has been easy to overlook becoming easy to see. You may find yourself at the center of a gathering, needed by many people at once, and your feelings about belonging run high: warmth at being among your people, or a sharpened sense of standing at the edge of the room. A long-held hope also checks in around now. The eleventh keeps your wishes for the future, and full light shows how a given wish is faring, closer than you thought, quietly outgrown, or waiting on a step only you can take. Across the chart the Sun holds the house of personal creativity and romance, so the axis stages its usual negotiation between the group and the individual heart: what the team needs against what you personally love, the shared plan against your own play. Both ends are yours. These few days reward showing up, finishing the collective thing, telling a friend what they are worth to you, and reading your hopes honestly rather than revising them on the spot. The tide then goes out on schedule. Returning yearly, this moon gives your social life an annual harvest, and over time it refines your answer to a durable question: which futures, and which people, you are actually building with.

Not every culmination has an audience. About once a year the Full Moon peaks in your twelfth house, the house of solitude, secrets, sleep and dreams, and everything you carry without showing, and the ripening happens out of sight. A Full Moon brings matters to fullness under maximum light; here the light shines into the one room of the chart that is usually dark. Feelings you have been holding privately, worry, grief, longing, an old guilt, rise to their full height in these few days, often without an obvious trigger, and dreams can turn loud and specific. Something hidden may complete: a private effort reaches its quiet end, a matter you have kept to yourself resolves, a thing done behind the scenes, by you or for you, comes to light. Sometimes what surfaces is simply tiredness, the accumulated cost of months of holding it together, presented all at once. The Sun meanwhile stands in your house of daily work and duty, and the axis presses its question: the schedule against the soul, what the calendar demands against what your inner life needs to stay honest. Around this moon the inner side pulls rank, and fighting it tends to go badly. What serves you is room: an empty evening, a long walk, sleep defended like an appointment, and if the feelings need a witness, one trusted person rather than a broadcast. Nothing about the height of the tide requires action; the twelfth house does its work through release, forgiveness, and rest, and much of what it completes was finished long before you noticed. When the light moves on, you re-enter the week lighter than you can quite account for. About once a year this house gets its hour of full light, and keeping the appointment teaches something the busy houses cannot: what surfaces in solitude is not an enemy, and tending the unseen part of your life is what keeps the visible part true.
